exemptions.subject: transistor-preamp-feedback
exemptions.why: The board was laid out by hand, built, and is in use. It predates the in-process stripboard layout system entirely and was never held to its placement rules, so a spot on it that routedUnderRigid or rigidOverlap refuses is a spot that was harder to build than it needed to be - not a defect to be fixed and not a counter-example to the rule.
exemptions.ownerWords: You should keep a record of exemptions. My ad-built boards should be exempt from the stricter standards of our new tooling—and, that exemption should carry a reason and provenance so we don't have to keep having this dumb conversation
doesNotExcuse: IT DOES NOT TRAVEL TO A BOARD THE TOOLING GENERATES. The subject is this one as-built artifact, named by the dump committed under boards/. A constructed seed, a candidate the search produces, and a board climbed FROM this one are each held to both rules in full: lib/stripboard/seed-place.ts refuses a placement that breaks either, lib/stripboard/moves.ts refuses a move that would, and nothing in lib/stripboard/ can read this file at all - it may not import from tools/ and tests/stripboard/model/no-fork.test.ts enforces that transitively.

IT DOES NOT EXCUSE ELECTRICAL SOUNDNESS, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT CLAIM ENTIRELY. violationsOf in lib/stripboard/invariants.ts - every reference net whole in one copper component, no component carrying two nets - is not exempted here and is not exemptable: an unsound start is refused rather than climbed from (lib/stripboard/search.ts), and this board passes it. An exemption is about how hard the board was to BUILD, never about whether it is the circuit.

IT DOES NOT EXCUSE HC1-HC10 OR ANY OTHER GATE. make check grades boards through tools/perfboard and tools/stripboard, which do not apply these two rules at all, so nothing in this file changes any verdict make check reaches. An exemption from a rule a gate does not run is not a licence over that gate.

IT DOES NOT MAKE THE VIOLATION INVISIBLE. An exempt subject does not fail and does not go quiet: every consultation that finds something returns an outcome of "exempt" carrying a one-line notice that names the board, the rule and the count, and the consumer reports it and proceeds. A silent exemption is a skipped check that looks like a passing one.

IT DOES NOT WEAKEN, NARROW OR REWORD EITHER RULE. routedUnderRigid and rigidOverlap in lib/stripboard/seed-area.ts are untouched by this file and are not reachable from it. The owner settled that direction before this registry existed: "my directives are more authoritative than a file on disk."
exemptions.note: [owner] 2026-10-15, granted in chat on his own instruction and recorded the same day. || OWNER'S WORDS (verbatim, and the whole of what he said in granting it): "You should keep a record of exemptions. The as-built diagram is instructive, but my directives are more authoritative than a file on disk." So the two halves are: his boards do not get to weaken the rules, AND the rules do not get to indict his boards. This file is the second half; lib/stripboard/seed-area.ts's comment is where the first half is recorded. || WHAT THIS EXEMPTION IS FOR, IN ONE SENTENCE: so that the question stops being re-litigated. The measurement had already been re-derived, re-argued and re-ruled on three times before it was written down as a grant, which is the "dumb conversation" his words name. || AGENT RATIONALE (written by an agent, not by the owner, and not endorsed by him): WHY A REGISTRY RATHER THAN A LINE IN A COMMENT. A prose exclusion is not consultable - nothing can ask it a question, nothing fails when it goes stale, and nothing notices when it is read by nobody. This file is loaded by tools/stripboard/exemptions.ts, every entry is answered as a VERDICT rather than a boolean, and tests/stripboard/exemptions.test.ts fails when an entry here is consulted by nothing. || WHAT WAS MEASURED, AND THE FIGURES ARE NOT KEPT HERE: on 2026-10-15 this board broke rigidOverlap in 2 places (Q1/RV3, rigid on rigid, where neither part can give way; and R4/RV4) and routedUnderRigid in 1 (R4's lower lead at strip 14, column 13, inside RV4's rectangle - under the RM-065's moulded body overhang, not between its terminals). THE AUTHORITY FOR THOSE COUNTS IS tests/stripboard/model/seed-room.test.ts, WHICH PINS THEM, and they are deliberately not carried as data in this file: a second place to keep a measured figure true is a place for it to go stale, and an exemption that silently stopped matching the board would be the worst of both. The figures appear in this note as context a reader needs, dated, and nothing reads them. || IT IS NOT A BLANKET AMNESTY FOR HAND-LAID BOARDS. pt2399-core and pultec-low-boost-frozen are also hand layouts of his and are NOT listed here: nothing currently measures either against these two rules, so an entry for them would be an exemption that fires on nothing, and the owner granted this one over the boards under discussion. If one of them is ever measured and the question arises, that is a new grant from him, not an extension somebody reads into this one.

notes.schema: [model] Schema 1, and the one loader that reads it is tools/stripboard/exemptions.ts. The shape follows stripboard/rules.json's convention - every entry carries its provenance, the owner's words verbatim, and an agent's rationale labelled as an agent's - for the reason that file gives: a decision with no recorded reason cannot be argued with, so the next reader re-derives it, and re-deriving a decision is how it gets quietly reversed. The two files are deliberately NOT merged: rules.json holds reviewed PARAMETERS the optimiser grades against, this one holds named EXCEPTIONS for specific artifacts, and a parameter set that carried its own exceptions would let an exception read as a weaker parameter.
notes.exemptions: [model] One entry per exempt subject, each with a single subject. An entry's id is how a notice cites it and must be unique; so must its subject, because two entries over one artifact would be two places to look for what it is excused from and the second would be found by nobody. THE LOADER REFUSES BY NAME RATHER THAN DEFAULTING, AND THE DIRECTION MATTERS: a missing or malformed entry, an unknown key, a rule outside the whitelist, a grantor who is not the owner, a consultedBy path that is not on disk - each is a refusal naming what is wrong and where, because the dangerous default here is "exempt". An exemption nobody can read is a nuisance; an exemption that appears out of a loader's charity is a gate that has been turned off by accident.
notes.from: [model] A rule may be exempted only if it is in EXEMPTABLE_RULES in tools/stripboard/exemptions-model.ts, which today names routedUnderRigid and rigidOverlap and nothing else. AN EMPTY-BY-DEFAULT WHITELIST THAT REFUSES LOUDLY IS THE POINT: adding a rule to it is a deliberate edit with a test beside it, never a silent widening, and the two hard placement rules are the only things the owner's grant was about. violationsOf is NOT in the whitelist and must not be added by anybody reading this file as precedent - it is electrical soundness, a different claim, and the registry refuses it by name so that the refusal teaches rather than merely blocks.
notes.grantedBy: [model] "owner" is the only admitted grantor, and the whitelist of one is the invariant rather than a formality: an agent may never author the acceptance criteria for the artifact it is producing (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-08-agent-authored-boards-design.md), and an agent that could grant an exemption from a criterion would be authoring the criterion by subtraction. Criteria reach an artifact through a rule file, a spec, or a reviewing agent that is never the one that authored it; so do exemptions from them.
